metadata.title: Brief von Stefan Zweig an Hannah; Altmann, Manfred Altmann [15. September 1940], SZ-AAL/B1.49

## Dieses Dokument

- Titel: Brief von Stefan Zweig an Hannah; Altmann, Manfred Altmann [15. September 1940], SZ-AAL/B1.49
- Signatur: SZ-AAL/B1.49
- Datum: 15.9.1940
- Objekttyp: Brief
- Umfang: 3 Scans

pages.transcription:
Dear Hannah and Manfred, it is not at all easy for us to write
to you. We read in the newspapers about the furious attacks on England
(happily also that they are rebated) and we feel ashamed to have here
such a perfect life. To look out of our windows is simply a dream, the
temperature is superb - a winter which is more June than May - the
people treat us in every possible way, we live quietly, deeply and the
most interesting life - really happy would it not be for you and all the
friends and the great misery of mankind. I will do everything to prolong
our stay here as Lotte will absolutely not leave, but I have to fulfil my
duties. I have a lecture in San Paolo this week, very well paid, 250
dollars and hotel and plane for us both, this covers alone one whole
month and I have no material worries as the lectures in Uruguay,
Argentine, Chile are equally well paid and we are invited in Uruguay
and Chile as guests of the Government, which will pay railway and
hotels. Next week we are going to the old towns in the interior of Brazil
as guest of the Province, poor Lotte will be photographed abundantly and
here you could see her in all the cinemas. Finally we go back to New York
we have already our visas and shall see (and let us hope so) and
fetch Eva. You may be both sure that we will look after her and
bring her back grown-up and perhaps with a Yankee-accent.
It is terrible for me to remember all the friends there over. I hope
that Robert Neumann and Korner[?] could leave, we have done all
for an American visa during my stay. Friedental I cannot help
from here except if he would like to go to Brazil or to Cuba - in
January I will try all possible. My former wife has her visas to
America and I believe also to Mexico, she is thanks to the help of
Ferro, who has been very kind to me, in Lisbon. But all the others. You
will understand how ashamed we feel here and I should be glad
to know that you can enjoy Bath in theses days of wrath. Please
be generous with money, nobody knows what the next years will
bring and I should be so glad to be of any help to you, to your
family and our friends. Yours
Stefan Zweig

[Randnotiz links:] Rio, 15. October Hotel Paysandu, after all
we cable yesterday
pages.notes: Handschriftlicher Brief von Stefan Zweig auf gelbem Papier. Die Randnotiz links ist vertikal geschrieben.
Rückseite des Dokuments, leer (durchscheinender Text der Vorderseite sichtbar).

result.confidence_notes: Der Text ist sehr gut lesbar. 'Korner[?]' ist eine unsichere Lesung eines Namens.
